summary.prose: Repo registration now stores a project type's typical build and test commands by itself, with no client prompt, and never overwrites or fails the add. The daemon owns the type table and the guarded writer; repo.settings.get gains a read-only buildSetup block. The terminal, VS Code and JetBrains Repo Configuration pages then show the Build rows as a section of their own, with the suggestion as the placeholder and a 'use suggested' action for repos with no commands. The work runs daemon first (t1, t2), then the shared fixture (t3), the three clients, and the docs.

tasks.title: Add buildSetupFor and applyBuildDefaults in the repo settings module; return buildSetup from repo.settings.get
tasks.summary: In src/daemon/repo-settings.ts add the types BuildSetup and BuildDefaultsOutcome, buildSetupFor(repoPath, entry) (project type from detectProjectType, commands source from the entry and the gate's profile rules, suggestion from PROJECT_TYPE_GUIDANCE only for python, go, rust and jvm with no commands) and applyBuildDefaults(repoPath, deps?) (reads the repo's own entry, writes the three keys in one writeKeys call only when none is set and the type has typical commands, never throws). repo.settings.get and repo.settings.set return payload.buildSetup. Nothing calls applyBuildDefaults yet.
acceptanceChecks: applyBuildDefaults writes typecheckCommand, testCommand and resultFormat 'exit-code' together for a Python, Go, Rust and JVM repo with no build key
It writes nothing for a Node repo, an unknown repo, and an entry that sets any one of the three keys, and reports the reason
It never throws: an unreadable entry or a failed write is { applied: false, reason: 'write-failed', note } and leaves no lone command
repo.settings.get returns buildSetup (type, commands source, suggestion for a repo with none, 'invalid' with a note for a bad entry) and writes nothing
Typecheck passes

tasks.title: Call applyBuildDefaults from repo.add as a guarded follow-up
tasks.summary: In the repo.add handler of src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts, after the registration and the indexing start, call applyBuildDefaults(normalisedPath) with the handler's own configPath and writer, guarded like the steering and MCP follow-ups, and return its outcome as buildDefaults in the result. A failure is logged and never fails the add; no client input is needed. Its tests are in src/daemon/__tests__/handler-runtime.test.ts and, for the gate reading a stored default as an ordinary setting, src/daemon/steps/build-step/__tests__/validate-task-round.test.ts.
acceptanceChecks: repo.add on a Python repo registers it, stores the default commands with no prompt and reports buildDefaults applied
repo.add on a repo whose entry already holds commands keeps them and reports already-set
A failing write still registers the repo and the add succeeds
A repo whose commands came from the add defaults is gated by those commands as an ordinary repo setting

tasks.summary: In the terminal settings modal (src/cli/panes/RepoSettingsModal.tsx) show the Build rows as a section of their own and, for a repo with commands source 'none' and a suggestion, offer an action that writes the three suggested values with repo.settings.set, clearing the first key when the second cannot be written (the LLD's lone-command rule). Nothing else about the modal changes.
acceptanceChecks: The modal shows the Build rows as a section of their own with the suggestion as the placeholder of an unset row
The 'use suggested' action is offered only when commands source is 'none' and a suggestion exists, and never for a repo that has commands

When the second write fails the first key is cleared and the reason is shown, so no lone command is left
The existing modal tests pass with the section
